text: Việt Nam urges SK Innovation to accelerate LNG power project

HÀ NỘI - Việt Nam has urged the Republic of Korea's SK Innovation to accelerate the development of the Quỳnh Lập LNG-fired power project in the central province of Nghệ An, as the country seeks to secure sufficient energy supplies to support its ambition of double-digit economic growth through 2030.
Permanent Deputy Prime Minister Phạm Gia Túc made the call at a meeting with Choo Hyeong Wook, president and CEO at SK Innovation, in Hà Nội on November 16.
Deputy PM Túc said securing energy supplies was an urgent priority for Việt Nam as the country pursued annual economic growth of at least 10 per cent through 2030.

The Government is therefore prioritising power projects capable of beginning operations before 2030, including the Quỳnh Lập LNG project which is being jointly developed by SK Innovation and PetroVietnam Power Corporation (PV Power).
The Government is also moving towards developing a competitive power generation market to enable capable investors to operate effectively in Việt Nam, he added.
During the meeting, Choo said SK Group planned to establish its Southeast Asian regional headquarters in Hà Nội to facilitate the expansion of its operations across the region.

Beyond the Quỳnh Lập project, SK Group is interested in developing integrated industrial-energy complexes in Việt Nam, using energy infrastructure as a foundation to attract investment in emerging technology, particularly artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres.
Choo said an integrated development model, rather than separate investments in individual projects, will strengthen links between energy infrastructure and technology operations.
The Quỳnh Lập LNG project could serve as the first model for this approach in Việt Nam.
He also called on Việt Nam to further improve policies to attract investment in emerging technology sectors, including regulations governing data, to facilitate business expansion.
In response, Deputy PM Túc said the Government supported the development of integrated energy hubs in line with national planning.

He said gas-fired power plants should be developed alongside gas-fired power centres and shared LNG storage infrastructure, rather than through fragmented investments by individual localities or businesses.
LNG storage facilities should be planned comprehensively to avoid duplication and inefficient use of resources.
Regarding energy hubs linked to AI and data centres, Túc stressed that a stable and reliable electricity supply would be essential to their operations.
Túc asked SK Group to prepare a comprehensive plan outlining its proposed investments in Việt Nam, with clear investment commitments and implementation timelines.
He said the Việt Nam stands ready to work closely with SK Innovation to address difficulties, while ensuring a balance of interests among relevant parties.

Việt Nam is restructuring its growth model around science, technology and innovation, in line with Resolution 57-NQ/TW adopted by the Politburo in December 2024, which identifies breakthroughs in science and technology, innovation and national digital transformation as key drivers of the country's development.

The Vietnammese Government is prioritising high-quality foreign investment projects that are environmentally friendly and generate high added value, Deputy PM Túc said, encouraging SK Innovation to expand its investments in green energy, green growth, AI and data centres.
Founded in 1953, SK Group is the Republic of Korea's second-largest conglomerate, with a market capitalisation of nearly US$200 billion.
Its main business areas include green energy, semiconductors and advanced materials, information technology and biotechnology. - VNS
